content.text: The thread shows SQU-125 through SQU-128 already have PRs, and SQU-129 was the active layer at the last checkpoint; SQU-130 to SQU-132 remain. I’m extracting the tracker rules and issue scope from the thread so the handoff can stand on its own without asking the next person to recover your private tracker context.

I read [Inkling UI Refactor Tracker SQU-124](t3-thread://v1/6c9fe016-4201-42c1-993a-44e3e00c936b) and captured the later issue comments so the handoff won’t depend on Linear. GitHub currently shows PRs [#131](https://github.com/Squidys-Tools/inkling/pull/131) and [#171](https://github.com/Squidys-Tools/inkling/pull/171) closed, and [#175](https://github.com/Squidys-Tools/inkling/pull/175), [#176](https://github.com/Squidys-Tools/inkling/pull/176), [#177](https://github.com/Squidys-Tools/inkling/pull/177), and [#178](https://github.com/Squidys-Tools/inkling/pull/178) open. The last chat checkpoint had SQU-129 partway through implementation and verification, with no PR yet.

Copy and paste this to Opus:

```text
Own and finish the Inkling UI refactor end to end: tracker SQU-124 and child issues SQU-125 through SQU-132. Work through the stack without pausing between layers for routine decisions. The project is squidys-tools/inkling, a local-first Windows Electron app with React, TypeScript, Vite, Node.js, and SQLite.

You do not have access to Linear, T3 Code, or the previous agent’s personal tools. Everything needed from the tracker is included below. Do not attempt to use Linear or claim that you updated issue statuses or comments. You may use the repository, normal Git/GitHub tools, and committed project scripts available in your environment. At the end, give the owner a paste-ready SQU-124 summary and recommended issue status updates.

## First: recover the actual working state

Read the repository’s `AGENTS.md` and relevant `package.json`, `t3.json`, and project docs. Treat the repo instructions as binding. This prompt also carries the important tracker comments and decisions for when Linear is unavailable.

Before changing files, inspect `git status`, the current branch, local worktrees, remotes, the current `main`, and the latest state of the existing pull requests. Preserve all existing task work. Never reset, clean, overwrite, or discard changes just to get a clean tree. Separate known refactor work from unrelated or unknown changes first.

Last recorded checkpoint, on 2026-10-22:

- SQU-125 had PR #175, SQU-126 had #176, SQU-127 had #177, and SQU-128 had #178. They were open at the last checkpoint; the thread recorded them as ready or marked ready after checks. Recheck live PRs, reviews, and CI before relying on any of that.
- The intended bases were #175 → `main`, #176 → `main`, #177 → #176, and #178 → #177. Do not duplicate an existing PR or branch. Fix valid review findings and maintain the stack if its branches still exist.
- SQU-129 was being implemented on the continuation branch/worktree, but had no PR yet. Its grid, card, dock, stage, and menu components had been written and wired into `App.tsx`; about 960 lines of matching CSS had been removed. Computed-style and visual comparisons looked close to the base, and the card-menu focus mismatch had been fixed. The full build, post-change benchmark, full-app pass, final checks, and PR were still outstanding at the last message. The before benchmark on that machine was: grid ready median 278 ms, click 360 ms, about 75 fps. The existing benchmark script measures `.library-scroll`; preserve that hook.
- The old worktree may contain SQU-129 changes not present on GitHub. Check for it or any supplied continuation branch before recreating work. If only the remote branches are available, the exact partial SQU-129 edits may be unrecoverable; continue from the #178 head and implement SQU-129 from the requirements below. Do not claim you recovered changes that are not there.
- PRs #131 and #171 were later closed without merging. The earlier brief said they gated the work, but the owner then resumed the goal and repeatedly said to continue; the previous agent proceeded through SQU-128 and into SQU-129. This handoff continues from that resumed state. Do not reopen, merge, rebase over, or discard #131 or #171, and do not stop solely because they remain closed without merging. Confirm #170 and #174 are still in `main`; use the actual current `main` as the parity baseline. Do not import behavior from closed PRs unless the owner separately approves it.
- The previous branch was named `t3/inkling-ui-refactor`; PR branch names and bases may have moved. Inspect rather than assuming.

The owner gave standing approval in the original task to open the specified PRs as drafts and mark them ready once verified and checks are green. There is no authorization to merge them. Do not merge any PR.

## Product rules and refactor constraints

This is a private visual library. Everything stays on the user’s machine. Capture must remain instant: save the card first and keep OCR, extraction, thumbnails, embeddings, and indexing in background jobs. Do not add network calls, analytics, uploads, synchronous processing during capture, new large IPC payloads, full-size assets where a thumbnail is enough, or work that makes the virtualized grid repaint on every keystroke.

Use hooks and small feature modules. No Zustand or TanStack Query. Keep Motion and GSAP for animation, sonner for toasts, `reader.css` as plain CSS because it styles untrusted article HTML, and onboarding keyframes in plain CSS. Do not add machinery for its own sake.

This is a parity port. Do not change visible behavior without owner sign-off. Do not fork the glass `Surface`; do not put glass or Base UI primitives inside grid cards. A shared visual primitive belongs in `src/ui/` and lands with its first consumer. `App.css` stays loaded until its final cleanup layer; remove only the blocks that have moved. Preserve licenses and attribution for vendored components.

Respect the performance and data-path work in #174: background-generated thumbnails and video posters, streamed assets, the windowed Archive, cached library size, and patching only the cards touched by completed jobs. Do not reintroduce full-list reloads. Keep `canvasImageCrossOrigin` on card and item-view images.

Keep comments sparse. Retain only short comments carrying an invariant, race/order guarantee, sanitization/security constraint, platform/runtime quirk, or dependency another file relies on. Remove narration, section labels, history, TODOs without an issue, and comments that restate the code. Keep license headers, lint directives, and knip tags.

Use the committed demo seed for UI checks. Never run against, write to, copy edits back to, or clean up the live library. For storage checks, use a scratch database created with SQLite backup semantics or `VACUUM INTO`. Do not hardcode local paths, ports, or model-cache paths. Track any server/process handle you start; never kill by process-name pattern. Do not use fixed sleeps as a readiness strategy.

Use the correct Bun version from `.bun-version` (1.4.2). The SQU-124 brief explicitly requires `bun run check` once per layer; this is a deliberate override of the general repo guidance against repo-wide checks. Run it for every layer, diagnose failures, and report them truthfully. The prior Windows run found a `storage.test.ts` “portable precedence” failure, a capture-server `EBUSY`, and CRLF lint errors in `.d.mts` files that were also present on `main`. Recheck these against the current clean baseline before calling them pre-existing. Do not say `bun run check` passed if it failed. Use green CI on the latest PR commit and the comparison to baseline to handle environment-specific failures.

Each UI PR needs before/after screenshots at the same viewport with the same demo seed, checked in both preview (CSS fallback) and the full app (liquid glass). Use the repository’s available verification harness. If WebGPU is unavailable, state that plainly and do not claim the liquid path was verified. Do not commit PR-only screenshots or videos. Upload evidence to the PR if GitHub access permits. Use a short video for motion in the final layer.

For each PR, say which applicable `AGENTS.md` “Hit every surface” entries were checked, including reverse paths. Be explicit about capture entry points, supported media kinds, search paths, preview/full-app coverage, and restore/close paths when they apply.

## Exact layer order and work

SQU-125 is independent and branches from `main`. SQU-126 targets `main`. Continue the UI stack linearly: SQU-127 from #176, SQU-128 from #177, SQU-129 from #178, then each next layer from the previous PR. Use the existing PRs if still present. Create one PR per issue, linked to its SQU key in the PR description. Draft PRs are authorized; mark ready only when the layer is verified and CI is green. Do not merge.

### SQU-125 — split `electron/storage.mjs` by domain

This layer already has PR #175; verify it rather than duplicating it.

Split the post-#174 storage implementation by domain while preserving behavior and the API used by `main.mjs`, `capture-server.mjs`, and tests. The existing work was described as a roughly 105-line `storage.mjs` entry over nine domain modules, with method bodies moved rather than rewritten.

Preserve the post-#174 `image_thumbnail` and `video_poster` jobs, idle backfill for existing videos, and single bounded query for item processing status. Capture must never resize. Leave `electron/asset-response.mjs` path containment and range handling alone. Migrations, lease recovery, and storage behavior must not change. Existing tests should only need import-path changes here; test pruning belongs in SQU-132. State which tests cover migrations and lease/recovery.

Use a scratch library only. The earlier full-app note-capture smoke check used a scratch library and passed; do not use live user data.

### SQU-126 — Tailwind v4, tokens, Base UI primitives, app shell

PR #176 exists. Keep Tailwind v4 through `@tailwindcss/vite`, without preflight. Build semantic `@theme` tokens from the existing `App.css` variables and merge duplicate aliases into one semantic set.

Add the first used `src/ui/` primitives: `Button`, `IconButton`, `Surface`, and `Tooltip`. `Surface` owns the `.glass` / `.css-glass` contract and fallback; do not duplicate the glass material per feature or change that contract without updating `LiquidGlass.tsx` and its tests. `App.css` stays loaded for unmigrated areas.

Move and restyle the titlebar, window controls, and sidebar. Preserve all shell behavior: sidebar close beside the wordmark; reopen from the toolbar glass button or the configured edge grip; Ctrl+\\ toggles it; Add sits at the sidebar foot and a round + appears in the toolbar when the sidebar is closed; the library slides over the sidebar. Preserve history navigation through mouse side buttons and Alt+Left/Right.

Base UI was already spiked successfully against the liquid glass and CSS fallback paths. Preserve these details:

- The app-wide tooltip is driven by `data-tooltip`, keeps its show delay and skip-delay between controls, and shows immediately on keyboard focus.
- Tooltips use liquid glass only over `.capture-bar` and `.view-dock`; use CSS glass elsewhere.
- Popups inside dialogs use `css-glass`; the liquid shape is drawn in the canvas plane and can appear dimmed beneath a dialog backdrop.
- Preserve visible focus rings. The global `:focus-visible` outline is unlayered; focused popups may need primitive-level outline handling.
- Dialog focus traps, Escape ordering, nested menu stacking, and focus return were checked. Preserve or improve them without changing normal behavior.

The window opens at 960×540. Use a fixed viewport for before/after shots. The sidebar/titlebar must match the baseline visually and remain keyboard accessible.

### SQU-127 — extract `App()` state into feature hooks

PR #177 exists. Keep `App()` as a composition shell; state belongs in focused `src/features/*` hooks. The app JSX and grid components are intentionally left for later layers, so do not force an arbitrary line-count target.

There are no pins in the current UI: do not add `usePins` or a pin write chain. Stored pin data remains untouched. Serendipity, Top of mind, and the back/forward toolbar are gone. The item view replaces the library frame instead of overlaying it.

Preserve these ordering and performance guarantees, with short comments where needed:

- Space moves apply only the latest generation.
- Membership reads drop stale results and cannot roll back a recent chip change.
- Latest-ref mirrors used by job callbacks remain intact.
- Finished jobs patch only touched cards through `src/lib/patchItems.ts`; skip fallback reload when nothing changed.
- Search stays debounced (200 ms as recorded in the PR) and does not re-render the grid on each keystroke.
- Do not add new global context or state libraries.

Tests for helpers are only needed if meaningful behavior was extracted as a pure function; do not add tests that merely mirror implementation or test trivial behavior.

### SQU-128 — capture bar and shortcuts

PR #178 exists. The capture modal was removed/folded into AddMenu; the layer covers the capture bar, shortcuts dialog, and AddMenu. Move the AddMenu’s `LICENSE.md` and attribution with the vendored component so the licenses page can include it.

Build `Dialog` and `SearchField` on Base UI. Preserve the idle search pill naming the current view, expansion on focus, shrink on Escape, and mascot search-eyes/bob. AddMenu is a morphing form panel; do not replace it with a menu just because a Menu primitive exists.

Keep every capture route behaviorally aligned: Add button, paste, drag and drop, clipboard, screenshot, deep link, URL/article, image, PDF, note, quote, video, X post, and miscellaneous file paths where supported. Capture stays instant; the backend search round trip remains debounced. Preserve the SQU-120 native folder-picker stacking fix and check that dialogs/search still respond after a native picker closes.

Verify dialog focus trap, Escape, backdrop close, and focus return. The prior PR recorded one difference from baseline: backdrop click now returns focus to the trigger, as Escape did. Treat that as part of the recorded implementation; do not introduce further interaction changes without approval.

### SQU-129 — library grid, cards, list view, filters

This is the next active layer. Extract the grid, all card variants, list view, selection ring, view dock, edge fade, and stage into `src/features/library/`. Serendipity is out of scope and must stay absent.

Cards remain plain elements inside virtualized masonry. No Base UI or glass surfaces in cards. Use Base UI Menu for the card context menu, but portal it outside the card/masonry. Preserve each type’s treatment and shared thumbnail logic in `ItemMedia.tsx` for article, image, PDF, video, post, note, quote, and file.

Keep archive tiles coherent with the current card implementation. Preserve the progressive edge blur from the vendored `components/GradualBlur/` plus `LibraryEdgeFade.tsx`, including its MIT + Commons Clause license. It sits behind the item view while the grid scrolls to frame edges. Preserve both Settings → Appearance view-dock styles using the vendored `SegmentedControl/` and its license. Preserve grid/list transition animations.

Keep card and item-view images’ `canvasImageCrossOrigin`. Video cards use a background-created poster or typed video art, never a `<video>` in the grid. Image cards show the original until their thumbnail job completes. Preserve `patchItems.ts` updates; do not reload the whole grid after background jobs.

Check every card kind, including imageless article/video, plain post, file, featured note, and processing/failed states. The demo seed lacked some of these, so the previous run temporarily added synthetic items to scratch copies for visual comparison; never leave test seed mutations in the product tree. Check grid, list, hover, selected, and empty states, plus Archive tiles, item-view art, onboarding artwork, dock styles, and context menu.

The previous before benchmark was 5/5 runs: 278 ms median until grid ready, 360 ms click, about 75 fps on that display. Run the same committed benchmark before/after under the same conditions and report both sets of numbers in the PR. Keep the `.library-scroll` selector working. Do not commit ad hoc benchmark output; only the repository’s allowed tracked benchmark files may change.

### SQU-130 — settings sheet and Archive

Extract Settings (General, Archive, Data, Extension, pairing, library makeup, Appearance, and Licenses) and Archive into `src/features/settings/`. Add Base UI `Tabs`, `Switch`, and needed form primitives with consumers. Build the Licenses filter menu on Base UI Menu. Preserve all Appearance options; it exists so maintainers can compare alternatives, not to pick a winner.

Preserve `ArchiveGrid.tsx` / `archiveGridWindow.ts` windowing and CSS grid layout, tab order, and selected behavior. Archive is read only while its tab is shown. The Archive count appearing only after the tab has first opened is a known gap; do not fix it here.

Settings reopens on Library, its first tab. Cached library size appears immediately and refreshes in background; do not regress commit `69e3641`. Hide optional version/size/last-copy facts when the backend cannot supply them in preview or full app.

Keep archive restore, selection mode, and delete working, with every reverse state verified. Export, import, and copy continue through the native picker; confirm dialogs still respond after the picker closes. Check tab keyboard navigation and focus return.

### SQU-131 — item view

Implement the current item view, which replaces the library frame. Do not port the obsolete overlay. Opening grows the card into the frame. Media uses a dotted stage; the right inspector contains title, note, Spaces, tags, details, and actions (move to Space, open original, archive). It closes only with Close or Escape.

There is no back/forward bar. Mouse side buttons and Alt+Left/Right still traverse opened-item history. Preserve zoom and pan, including pixel zoom; never add a drop shadow to the scaled image. Keep live Space-chip membership and stale-read protection. Preserve the lazy note editor and PDF viewer chunks, including their warm-up behavior. Verify every kind: article, image, PDF, video, post, note, quote, and file. Verify reverse actions. Keep the mascot in the inspector corner and `canvasImageCrossOrigin` on `ItemMedia` images. Preserve the note editor’s full height in narrow windows.

Use `Tabs` and `Menu` primitives where called for, restyle with Tailwind, and remove only the matching item-view / Similar-tab CSS. Fold in `PdfViewer.tsx` if it fits the shared Dialog cleanly without widening scope.

### SQU-132 — onboarding, reader, cleanup, final layer

Move remaining CSS to its owner: onboarding keyframes and GSAP selectors beside `FirstRunOverlay` / `components/onboarding/*`, toast styling beside the Toaster, and then delete `App.css`. `reader.css` remains plain CSS beside `ReaderView` because it styles untrusted article HTML through descendant selectors. Use shared tokens there.

Move only onboarding CSS and keyframes; the onboarding screens, order, and mascot rhythm are product intent and must not change. Preserve reader HTML sanitization.

Check for remaining UI god files (roughly over 600 lines without a reason) and split only where the existing scope requires it. Update `docs/tech-stack.md` and `docs/design.md` to match reality and describe the liquid glass WebGPU canvas, `.glass`/`.css-glass` contract, and CSS fallback in preview / machines without WebGPU. Remove or justify stale Zustand/TanStack Query claims. Rewrite existing documentation instead of appending duplicate explanations. Add one `docs/changelog.md` line under Changed referencing SQU-124, following the file’s own rules. Update `t3.json`, `knip.json`, and `biome.jsonc` if scripts, entries, or ignores changed.

Test pruning is explicitly in scope only here. Across `src/` and `electron/`, remove type-redundant checks, trivial logic tests, basic DOM behavior, static-markup renders, mock-call mirrors, smoke tests, duplicate table rows, and wall-clock/performance asserts. Keep tests for extraction/sanitization/embed allowlists, OCR scoring, queue leases/recovery, migrations/persistence, asset path containment/range requests, deep links/external-format parsing, ordering/races, `liquidGlassShape`, and tests added by fix commits. Mark a regression test `// regression: #NNN` if its name does not make that clear. Remove helpers/fixtures/exports used only by deleted tests, without changing product code for the pruning. No custom lint rules for comments/tests.

Report before/after test counts and `bun test` duration in the PR. Finish with a full-app walkthrough of every surface; include a short video for motion. `App.css` must be gone and the final `bun run check` must pass (with any true environment limitations plainly reported).

## Per-layer completion

For every child layer:

1. Read the current code and its existing PR/review comments; use the tracker requirements above where Linear would normally be needed.
2. Make the smallest change that completes the layer and preserves current-main behavior.
3. Run the required per-layer checks, including `bun run check`; targeted checks as useful. Verify in preview and full app for UI layers. Capture and attach same-seed, same-viewport before/after evidence.
4. Review the actual diff for accidental behavior changes, duplicate CSS, comment quality, license movement, and any damage to performance/data paths.
5. Commit with a conventional title, push only the branch you own, and create/update the one PR for that issue if GitHub access is available. Include the SQU key, checks, surface coverage, reverse paths, visual evidence, and benchmark where applicable. Mark ready only after verification and green latest-commit CI. Never merge.
6. Continue to the next layer.

Do not stop to ask about choices already decided above. Stop and report only for a genuinely destructive or live-library operation, a rule conflict that cannot be resolved from this prompt and repository, a behavior change needing owner sign-off, Base UI failing to coexist with glass after a real spike, or a CI failure you cannot attribute after a real diagnostic attempt. If something is unavailable due to this environment (Linear, personal scripts, WebGPU, full app, GitHub write access), state exactly what could not be verified or updated and continue all independent work.

## Final handoff

When implementation is complete, provide a concise report with:

- PR links, bases, current CI/review state, and commits for SQU-125 through SQU-132.
- Checks and real-app/preview verification for each layer; list any baseline failures or unavailable evidence without calling them passes.
- SQU-129 before/after benchmark numbers.
- Test counts and `bun test` duration before/after SQU-132 pruning.
- Any known follow-ups and an exact paste-ready summary comment for SQU-124. Do not claim to have posted it or changed Linear statuses.
```
